title: Vitryne format v1: project.json
description: The root of a project file: which garments, on which avatar, with which fabrics, appearances and simulation settings. Each entity lives in its own part: garments/<id>.json, fabrics/<id>.json, appearances/<id>.json, avatars/<id>/avatar.json.

garments.description: Garment ids, in layering order: the first is worn closest to the body.

avatar.description: The avatar the garments are draped on.

fabrics.description: Every fabric in the project, used or not (the project's own library).

appearances.description: Every appearance in the project, used or not. Absent: none.

pose.description: The pose the avatar is draped in (version 7). Absent: the avatar's rest pose. A pose made for another avatar than `avatar` is stale and ignored.
A turn for some joints of an avatar's skeleton (the skin in its body.glb).

avatar.description: The avatar the pose was made for.

joints.description: Joint name (as in the avatar's skin) to a unit quaternion [x, y, z, w]: the joint's turn about its own head, in the frame of the joint above it. A joint not listed is at rest.

simulation.description: How the drape is computed. Garments may override any of it (garment.simulation).

targetVertices.description: Mesh resolution: about this many cloth vertices per garment.

engine.description: Engine tuning, sparse: only values that differ from the engine's defaults. Keys and units are the engine's own (vitryne-solver SimSettings field names, SI, metres): this object is the one exception to the format's mm rule. Unknown keys are preserved and ignored.
